questions.question: Describe how a PAT model is evaluated against its specifications and constraints, what the evaluation sheet records, and what it means to evaluate objectively, fairly, accurately and in depth.
questions.expected_answer: Each specification and constraint from the design step becomes a test: hang the stated load and measure the lift, push the top sideways, measure the overall size, check that moving parts are enclosed. The sheet records each specification or constraint, the test, the result (met, partly met, not met) and the evidence observed, followed by paragraphs on strengths with reasons, weaknesses with their probable causes traced to design or making decisions, and specific improvements. Objectively means judging by test rather than opinion; fairly means recording strengths and weaknesses both; accurately means using measurements; in depth means tracing causes and proposing fixes, and reflecting on the process.

questions.question: Explain the method for evaluating a complex structure or another team's model fairly, and give an example of a useful peer evaluation comment.
questions.expected_answer: State the structure's purpose; list advantages and disadvantages under the same headings for every structure (does the job, material and cost, safety, durability, appearance, impact on people and environment), at least two points each; judge whether advantages outweigh disadvantages for that purpose and what you would change. Describe what was observed before judging, give the structural reason in course vocabulary, and pair each weakness with a strength. Example: 'When the crank was turned under load the top moved about 20 mm sideways because the front panel has no diagonal and is an unbraced rectangle; the wide base kept it from tipping.'

questions.question: Outline the structure of the team presentation, state how the work is shared and how visual material and the model are used, and give four delivery rules.
questions.expected_answer: Follow IDMEC: scenario and brief; investigation and where ideas came from; chosen design on the working drawing and artist's impression with reasons for rejecting alternatives; making with photographs and sequence; evaluation results against each specification; proposed improvements; then questions. Every member presents one step and can answer questions on any part. Drawings, sketches and the evaluation table are displayed large enough for the back row and pointed to, not read aloud; the model is demonstrated live with one member responsible for steadying it, and any failure is explained using the evaluation. Delivery: face the audience, speak slowly and clearly, keep to time (about five minutes plus questions) after rehearsing with a timer, use technical terms with a short explanation, and state weaknesses before the audience does.
